name: Mango Pickle
subtitle: raw mango cured in salt then packed with mustard, fennel and oil

ingredients.qty: 1kg firm and sour, cut into 2cm pieces with the stone shell

ingredients.note: the preservative, so do not reduce it

prepNotes: Everything must be bone dry: the mango, the jar, the spoon, your hands. A single drop of water is how a pickle grows mould.
The first salting draws out the water that would otherwise spoil it. Do not shorten it.

steps.text: Wash and dry the mango pieces thoroughly, then spread them on a cloth for 2 hours until the surface is completely dry.
steps.tip: Completely dry. This is not a step to rush.

steps.text: Toss with the salt and turmeric, pack into a dry jar, and leave 2 days, shaking daily.
Drain off the liquid that has collected and dry the pieces again in the sun or a low oven for an hour.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking, then cool it completely.
steps.tip: Smoking then cooled: raw mustard oil is harsh and can spoil the pickle.

steps.text: Mix the ground spices, nigella and asafoetida with the mango, then pour over enough cooled oil to submerge everything.
Seal and leave in the sun 7 to 10 days, shaking daily, until the mango softens and darkens.
steps.tip: The oil must always sit above the mango. Top it up if the level drops.

storage: Keeps a year in a cool dark place if the oil covers the pickle and only a dry spoon ever goes in. Refrigeration is unnecessary and dulls it.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
